sentences.text:
Aloke Kumar Ghosh vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 27 April,
2016

Author: Joymalya Bagchi
Bench: Joymalya Bagchi

In The High Court At Calcutta Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Present:
The Hon'ble Justice Joymalya Bagchi C.R.R. 1664 of 1998 Aloke Kumar Ghosh
-Vs-
State of West Bengal & Anr.

For the Petitioner : Mr. Swapan Mullick,
 Mr. Jagatbandhu Roy,
 Ms. Manasi Roy
For the State : Mr. Manjit Singh ...

Ld. Public Prosecutor
 Mr. Pawan Gupta
Heard on : 27.04.2016
Judgement on: 27.04.2016

Joymalya Bagchi, J. :-
Judgement and order dated 29th May, 1998 passed by the learned Additional
Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Bankura in Criminal Appeal No. 27 of 1995 affirming the
judgment and order dated 12th September, 1995 convicting the appellant for
commission of offence punishable under Sections 7(1)/16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of
Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentencing him of suffer rigorous imprisonment for
six months and to pay a fine of Rs.1000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment
for further one month has been assailed.

The prosecution case as alleged against the petitioner is to the effect that on 31st August, 1992 at 11 A.M., the complainant along with others had come to Premises No.
183B, Dalmadal Road, Rashtala, Bishnupur and found the petitioner was selling grocery items including chilli powder.

Chilli powder contained in polythene packet,
each weighing 50 gms., branded as 'Guin Spices', manufactured by Guin Traders,

sentences.text: On demand, the petitioner was unable to produce food licence and the complainant collected chilli powder samples of 450 gms. amounting to Rs.22.50p suspecting it to be adulterated.
Notice was issued upon the petitioner.
Sale receipts were also seized.
It is the prosecution case that the petitioner was unable to produce any warranty for purchase of chilli powder at the time of inspection.
It is alleged that report of public analyst showed that the chilli powder was adulterated and misbranded.
On the basis of complaint lodged by PW1, trial commenced against the petitioner and one Madan Ghosh, owner of the shop.
In conclusion of trial, petitioner was convicted and sentenced but co-accused Madan Ghosh was acquitted.
In appeal, the said conviction and sentence was upheld.
Hence, the present revision.

Mr. Swapan Mullick, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the courts below did not consider the cash memo which was exhibited in the instant case and which showed that the articles had been purchased from DW1.
He further submitted that the report of public analyst (Exhibit-13) does not establish that the seized article is adulterated.
I have considered the materials on record.
I find that DW1 has not supported the defence of the petitioner that he had sold the packets of chilli powder to the petitioner and hence, no case of warranty has been established by the petitioner.
Coming to the public analyst report, however, I find that the said report is vague and non-specific in nature and does not disclose the nature of adulteration beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I hold that the prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence, I set aside the impugned judgement and order of conviction and sentence.
The revision petition is allowed.
Photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the parties on priority basis on compliance of all formalities.
(Joymalya Bagchi, J.) akd Aloke Kumar Ghosh vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 27 April, 2016
